results.answer: Skipping this month means the next instalment will not be taken, and the SIP will continue as normal from the following month. Your previously bought units stay invested and keep moving with the market.
Cancelling stops future instalments but the money already invested stays in the fund and continues to move with the market.
If an auto‑debit fails, the fund house does not charge a penalty, but your bank may levy a fee for the failed debit. Several consecutive failures could lead the fund house to cancel the SIP.
In this demo you can pause a SIP for 1 to 3 months. After the pause period the SIP restarts automatically at the same amount.
Yes, after you pause a SIP it will automatically restart on its own after the pause period ends.
You can lower the SIP amount to as low as the fund's minimum, which in this demo is ₹100 per month.
Yes, after cancelling a SIP you can start a new one later, which may require a new mandate. Your previously invested units stay invested and continue moving with the market.
Stopping a SIP does not trigger any tax; tax applies only when you redeem (sell) units.
Pausing a SIP does not attract any exit load; exit load applies only when you redeem units.

Cancelling the mandate at your bank stops the automatic debits, so the next SIP instalment will fail unless you set up a new mandate or change the SIP in the app. The already bought units remain invested and continue to move with the market. You can restart the SIP by creating a new mandate or adjusting it in the app.
If you pause today, the request may take a few working days, so the instalment scheduled for tomorrow could still be processed.
Yes, lowering the amount keeps the SIP active as long as the new amount is above the minimum (₹100 in this demo). The SIP continues with the reduced instalment while existing units stay invested.
